blurb: Apple platforms use a hardware True Random Number Generator (TRNG) integrated into the Secure Enclave as the root entropy source. The operating system's /dev/random kernel interface seeds its internal CSPRNG with TRNG output, combined with additional entropy from interrupt timing, device sensor data, and other environmental sources. This cryptographically secure random output is used for generating encryption keys, authentication protocol nonces, ASLR address space randomization, unique identifiers, and all other cryptographic operations requiring high-quality unpredictable values across every Apple platform.
